title: Mantoobaugs
summary: Mantoobaugs is Tooker's name for a reserved parcel on Hashamomuk Neck in Southold, associated with swamps, corn fields, and the Five Wigwams area. The blue marker is approximate.
address_label: General Hashamomuk Neck / Arshamomaque area near Greenport
map_geometry_source: Approximate Hashamomuk Neck / Arshamomaque location based on Tooker and related Manhansuck/Hashamomuk entries; offset slightly for map visibility.
introduction_content: Mantoobaugs is a Southold placename placed on Hashamomuk Neck, near the broader Arshamomaque and Greenport area. The name is tied to a reserved parcel of land adjoining two swamps.
translation_content:
Mantoobaugs is treated as a possessive place-name, probably connected with an Indigenous person named Mantoobang. The place is interpreted as Mantoobang's plantation or corn fields rather than as a translated landscape term.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names reveal how people refer to, relate to, and know a landscape.”

— Anchorage Museum Education Department, Anchorage Maps and Place Names lesson plan (2020), lesson introduction
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is placed generally in the Hashamomuk Neck / Arshamomaque area near Greenport and is offset slightly from related markers for map visibility, not an exact reconstruction of the reserved parcel or swamp locations.
